issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency for the Developer instance method that produces a printable Swift experience description. The problem statement and the template declare/require a method named swiftExperienceDescription() (problem statement: problem_statement.md lines 35-41; template extension signature: Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift line 24). The solution implementation defines the method as getExperienceDescription() (solution Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift line 24) and the Developer initializer in the solution calls getExperienceDescription(). Meanwhile the solution's Client calls swiftExperienceDescription() (solution Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift lines 26-27). This mismatch (expected name swiftExperienceDescription vs implemented name getExperienceDescription) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about which method name to implement and call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Preferably rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription() and update its internal calls (e.g., the initializer) to call swiftExperienceDescription(), and ensure Client.swift calls the same name. Alternatively, if you prefer getExperienceDescription(), update the problem statement, template extension, and Client to reference getExperienceDescription(). Apply the same identifier in the template, solution, and client to avoid compilation errors and student confusion.
